item.title: Python random.shuffle vs creating a new shuffled list
item.description:
“Python random.shuffle vs creating a new shuffled list”

Why does the Python standard library function random.shuffle(x) alter the list x directly, returning None, and what are the preferred techniques for generating a new, independently shuffled sequence when the original must remain intact?

The In-Place Nature of random.shuffle()

The primary mechanism for randomizing sequence order in Python’s random module is random.shuffle(). A key characteristic of this function, shared by many Python API methods that mutate containers, is that it operates in-place and signals this by returning None.
